audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows read 'Skill' regardless of what their why text says, level 3 included, and the first-item row gave Sylas a spike its own content why hands to Neeko.
audit.why: The packet chart and the mirror neeko__sylas both read Skill / Skill / Neeko / Skill / Neeko / Skill / Sylas. Neeko owns level 3 (Q-E-Q from 800-1000 range against a melee with one 400-range dash) and level 6 (Pop Blossom's wind-up is hidden by her disguise); Sylas takes the two-item row.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 6, first item and 2+ items flipped in matched phases[].side + win[] pairs, ratings moved, and the three contradicting why lines rewritten.

audit.why: Four spikes in the right order — her level 3 combo, her level 6 ultimate as the steal target, her first-item burst, and Sylas's two-item brawl. Only the ultimate's name was wrong inside spikes[1].
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text renamed to Pop Blossom with its real 120/105/90s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Shapesplitter Pop' is not an ability — it appears in whys[4], spikes[1] context, wants.you[2] and late. wants.foe[2] calls the clone 'W Mimic'. The late text says a Sylas holding her R can disguise as a teammate. Four fields also say Abduct stuns.
audit.why: Her ultimate is Pop Blossom (600 range, 120/105/90s): a leap that knocks up nearby enemies and stuns them on landing, with the preparation hidden while she is disguised. Shapesplitter is the W (16-12s) — the clone plus every-third-attack bonus damage. The disguise is Inherent Glamour, her passive; Hijack copies only the ultimate, so Sylas gets the leap and the stun and never the disguise. Abduct is a chain pull with no stun.
audit.corrected: Real names used, the disguise claim removed from the late text, and the actual value of the steal stated — knockup into stun, not an invisible opener.

audit.why: Tangle-Barbs at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s is correctly identified as the cooldown the lane runs on, and every dos/donts entry keys off it.

edits.before: Full kit: E2 chain into Q-W-AA is a real chunk, and E1's shield eats the counter-trade. Trade in full rotations.
edits.after: Her Q-E-Q lands from 800-1000 range and Tangle-Barbs roots the dash — you have one 400-range approach and she owns it.

edits.before: Hijack online — you now own a copy of Neeko's ultimate. The all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way.
edits.after: Pop Blossom's wind-up is hidden while she is disguised — her six arrives with no tell, and yours needs her to cast first.

edits.before: Riftmaker spike — your full chain with the W heal wins almost any extended 1v1 that starts even.
edits.after: Riftmaker heals through her poke, but Shadowflame one-rotates you through it — whoever lands first wins.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — Abduct only pulls you in, and a melee mage has no exit without it.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Abduct does not stun — it pulls you to her, straight into the Tangle-Barbs root you were trying to dodge.

edits.before: Her R Shapesplitter Pop is a disguised AoE ground-stun with massive burst — in Sylas's hands it is a clean teamfight initiator, so stealing it immediately swings the lane dynamic.
edits.after: Pop Blossom knocks up everything nearby and stuns it on landing, and her disguise hides the wind-up — at six she opens from a fake ally with no tell for you to read.

edits.before: Neeko's R is one of the best things Sylas can steal — a disguised ground-slam AoE stun that wins teamfights, so look for the first R theft the moment she uses it aggressively.
edits.after: Pop Blossom is one of the best things Sylas can steal — a leap that knocks up and then stuns everything nearby, so Hijack it the moment she spends her own 90-120s copy.

edits.before: Steal her R Shapesplitter Pop and use it as an initiating AoE stun so her main teamfight tool works for you instead
edits.after: Steal Pop Blossom and open fights with it — the knockup into stun is her best tool and Hijack recharges in 30-80s

edits.before: Clone-swap with W Mimic before your E lands so you hook the decoy and waste your engage window
edits.after: Send a Shapesplitter clone before your E lands so you chain the decoy and waste the engage

edits.before: Late game Sylas holding Neeko's R Shapesplitter Pop is a genuine teamfight threat — you can disguise as a teammate and then detonate the stun on a clustered enemy team exactly as she would. Your Riftmaker sustain means you survive one rotation if you go in at full HP, and Petricite Burst autos in extended brawls let you shred her once she has no flash. The lane is even overall; your job is to be alive at 6 with enough gold for a first item, steal her R every time she gives you the chance, and translate that into objective fights where the AoE stun is worth more than anything she can do herself.
edits.after: Late game Sylas holding Pop Blossom is a genuine teamfight threat — Hijack copies the leap, the knockup and the landing stun, though not her disguise, so you enter on your own terms with Abscond instead. Your Riftmaker sustain means you survive one rotation if you go in at full HP, and Petricite Burst autos in extended brawls let you shred her once she has no flash. The lane is even overall; your job is to be alive at 6 with enough gold for a first item, steal her R every time she gives you the chance, and translate that into objective fights where the stun is worth more than anything she can do herself.
